body:
## What is this PR about?

Fixes #3710, where a project with **Trigger Type = "On tag"** still builds on every regular commit/push (and real tag pushes don't deploy).

The GitHub **App** webhook handler (`pages/api/deploy/github.ts`) already respects `triggerType`. But the **refresh-token** webhook handlers — the URL Dokploy shows for manual webhook setup — never looked at it:

- `apps/dokploy/pages/api/deploy/[refreshToken].ts` (applications)
- `apps/dokploy/pages/api/deploy/compose/[refreshToken].ts` (compose)

For a GitHub source they only checked `watchPaths` + branch match, so:
1. A `triggerType: "tag"` app/compose **still deployed on every branch push** — the field was ignored (the exact bug reported, on Docker Compose).
2. A real tag push (`ref = refs/tags/x`, which `extractBranchName` leaves unstripped) failed the branch match → **tag pushes never deployed** via this path.

### Change

- Add an exported `extractTagName` helper in `[refreshToken].ts` (detects tag events for GitHub/Gitea/GitLab/Bitbucket).
- Gate the `sourceType === "github"` branch of both handlers on `triggerType`, mirroring `github.ts` semantics:
  - **tag**: deploy only on tag events (skip branch/watchPaths — tags aren't branch-scoped and the UI hides watchPaths for tags), titled `Tag created: <tag>`; ignore non-tag pushes.
  - **push** (default): ignore tag events; keep the existing branch + watchPaths checks unchanged.

Scope is **GitHub only**, matching the issue and the original feature (PR #1613). No schema, migration, or UI changes — the `triggerType` column and GitHub UI selector already exist.

## Checklist

- [x] You created a dedicated branch based on the `canary` branch.
- [x] You have read the suggestions in the CONTRIBUTING.md file.
- [x] You have tested this PR in your local instance.

Testing: added `extractTagName` unit tests in `__test__/deploy/github.test.ts` (40/40 pass) and verified `biome check` is clean on the touched files. Also exercised the handlers manually against a local instance with simulated branch-push vs tag-push payloads for both `triggerType` settings.

## Issues related (if applicable)

closes #3710

body:
## What

Adds a fourth experience to interview-sim: a **guided Python course** for experienced programmers who are new to Python (they already know TS/JS/Java/Go). It reuses the voice-loop + code-window setup — a voice **tutor** teaches each lesson conversationally, watches your code and run output live, and walks you through hands-on exercises. The goal is job-ready Python: syntax, idioms, tooling, and the libraries you'll meet day one.

Design spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-12-python-learning-mode-design.md`.

## Architecture — a fourth mode on the existing rails

The mode union is the dispatch table; learning is one more row. **`/api/chat` doesn't change at all** — the lesson script arrives via the existing `questionPrompt` field, and editor state rides the existing context plumbing.

- `SessionMode = InterviewMode | "learning"` added only at the shared voice-loop boundary. `InterviewMode` stays the three graded modes (it still exhaustively keys `SCORE_LABELS`).
- `src/lib/lessons/` mirrors `src/lib/problems/`: per-module files → `index.ts` (`MODULES`, `LESSONS`, `getLesson`). `buildLessonScript()` serializes a lesson into the tutor's per-turn context.
- Tutor system/kickoff prompts; a **non-graded recap** (not a scorecard) via the existing `/api/assess` pipeline → new `RecapCard`.
- `/learn` overview + `/learn/[lessonId]` workspace (`LessonWorkspace`); exercise advancement is **user-controlled** (Prev/Next) — the LLM never drives UI state.
- One-line runner change (`loadPackagesFromImports`) so numpy/pandas lessons run in-browser via Pyodide.
- Honest renames for things now shared by a non-interview: `useInterviewSession` → `useSession<T>`, `InterviewContext` → `SessionContext`, `/api/assess` returns `{ result }`.

## Curriculum

8 modules / 25 lessons / 69 exercises, written for experienced programmers (leads with Python specifics + explicit contrasts to other languages):
Python in an Afternoon · Core Data Structures · Pythonic Idioms · Objects & Typing · Stdlib Power Tools · Errors & Testing · Environment & Tooling (conversational) · Common Libraries (requests/numpy/pandas).

## How the content was authored

A parallel agent workflow (`scripts/author-lessons.workflow.js`) authored each module, then **adversarially reviewed** it — the review caught three genuinely broken teaching examples the authors missed (a `NameError` swap, a missing `field` import in a dataclass example, a bogus TypeScript `int` contrast). Content is generated deterministically from the verified JSON by `scripts/gen-lessons.mjs`.

## Verification — all green

- **Run-every-scaffold gate:** all 69 exercise starters execute clean under `python3` (numpy/pandas under an isolated venv) — `scripts/run-lesson-gate.mjs`
- `lessons.test.ts` invariants (25 lessons, 8 modules, globally unique ids)
- `tsc` (0 errors), `eslint` (0 errors), `vitest` (73 tests pass), `next build` (✓ both `/learn` routes)
- All existing interview modes and their 67 prior tests are unaffected.

## Added — Finance & Controlling (the v0.2.0 module)

- **Bank reconciliation** — CSV statement import (background job over 1k lines), set-based match suggestions, suspense clearing ([#36](https://github.com/Taha-Mahmoodi/atlas-erp/pull/36))

body:
A correctness pass on the shell-hook work, plus the explicit-export regression introduced in 0.13.0. Six items (the four you flagged + the two prior approvals):

## Changed
**Decouple `env export` from `scope`.** 0.13.0 gated *all* `env export`, which broke `eval "$(envpkt env export)"` setups that load secrets at login. Now:
- **plain `env export`** (explicit) emits everything, like 0.12.0 — never silently withholds;
- **`env export --track`** (the hook's ambient path) respects `scope` (exec withholds secrets, shell emits).

This is the real fix for the regression — you don't even need the `scope = "shell"` line on a global package for explicit export to work (though it's still correct to have).

## Fixed
- **Missing-key errors now surface on `cd`.** The hook no longer `2>/dev/null`s the inject, and `env export --track` is quiet on success — so a `SealKeyUnavailable` prints on `cd` (realizing B1 through the hook, which the plan claimed but the code muted). `formatError` now renders that error with the searched key paths + remediation, not just the bare tag.
- **bash array `PROMPT_COMMAND`** (bash ≥5.1): appends to the array instead of string-concatenating (which dropped all but element 0).

## Added

body:
Resolves #13052

Authored by GPT-5.5 (Codex Desktop). Session 019ebe4d-0687-7dd2-8e37-c48ac8e057ad.

Guards `checkout_pull_request` so a shared github-workflow MCP server can no longer silently mutate its own checkout while telling the caller that their workspace was checked out. The tool now requires an explicit caller git-root `repoPath`, verifies that path is the git top-level, runs `gh pr checkout` only there, and returns read-back `{repoPath, branch, headSha}` for reviewer V-B-A. Missing caller workspace data now returns `CALLER_WORKSPACE_REQUIRED` instead of attempting a server-root checkout.

Evidence: L2 (focused unit coverage for refusal, repoPath validation, checkout read-back state, and gh failure shape; static schema/code checks) -> L2 required (tool-contract ACs are unit-coverable). Residual: post-merge MCP reload/live tool validation.

## Deltas from ticket

- Chose the explicit `repoPath` mechanism from #13052 rather than a session-registered workspace. MCP transport still does not carry caller cwd, so explicit caller workspace is the narrow honest contract.
- Legacy numeric calls are preserved at the JS method boundary only to return an explicit `CALLER_WORKSPACE_REQUIRED` refusal; they no longer mutate `aiConfig.projectRoot`.
- The reviewer-side guard is intentionally temporary: the `pr-review` guide now requires manual HEAD-vs-current-PR verification until review tooling consumes the returned `{repoPath, branch, headSha}` automatically.
- Sibling sweep disposition: `get_pull_request_diff` remains read-only; `manage_pr_reviewers` and issue assignee mutations are remote GitHub state changes, not local worktree mutations; `sync_all` is the existing content-sync exception with a dev-branch precondition and is outside this checkout-review path.

## Substrate Slot Rationale

- `.agents/skills/pr-review/references/pr-review-guide.md`: rewrite of one existing Empirical Checkout Mandate sentence. Disposition `compress-to-trigger`: only loaded during PR review, high trigger frequency, high failure severity, high enforceability. Explicit sunset is embedded in the line.
- `learn/agentos/GitHubWorkflow.md`: rewrite of tool documentation so public docs match the new explicit-caller-workspace contract. Disposition `rewrite`: no new process gate, just stale-contract correction.
- `ai/mcp/server/github-workflow/openapi.yaml`: tool-contract schema update for `repoPath` and the verifiable response shape; this is the MCP source surface, not free-form guidance.

Decision Record impact: aligned-with ADR 0019. The fix keeps `aiConfig.projectRoot` as server diagnostic context only and does not introduce a second config source of truth.

## Test Evidence

- `node --check ai/mcp/server/github-workflow/server.mjs` passed.
- `node --check ai/services/github-workflow/PullRequestService.mjs` passed.
- `node --check test/playwright/unit/ai/services/github-workflow/PullRequestService.spec.mjs` passed.
- `git diff --check origin/dev...HEAD` passed.
- `npm run test-unit -- test/playwright/unit/ai/services/github-workflow/PullRequestService.spec.mjs -g "checkoutPullRequest"` -> 4 passed.
- Full local `PullRequestService.spec.mjs` note: 41/44 passed; the remaining 3 local failures are pre-existing `getPullRequestDiff` cases that shell out to unauthenticated `gh pr view/diff` in the isolated temp worktree. The focused checkout contract tests pass.
- Branch-history close-keyword check: `git log origin/dev..HEAD --format=...` contains only `91cdac1cf fix(ai): guard checkout_pull_request workspace mutation (#13052)` and no extra close targets.

## Post-Merge Validation

- [ ] Reload the github-workflow MCP server and call `checkout_pull_request` without `repoPath`; expect `CALLER_WORKSPACE_REQUIRED` and no branch mutation.
- [ ] Call `checkout_pull_request` with an explicit disposable caller git-root `repoPath`; verify returned `headSha` matches the current PR head before running related tests.
- [ ] Once review tooling consumes returned `headSha`, remove the temporary manual HEAD-verification sentence from the `pr-review` guide.

- `91cdac1cf` — `fix(ai): guard checkout_pull_request workspace mutation (#13052)`

Publication was initially blocked because the temp worktree shell lacked the `GH_TOKEN` environment even though the shared checkout shell had valid `gh api` identity as `neo-gpt`. The branch was finally published by running the push from the authenticated shared-checkout environment while targeting the temp worktree with `git -C`.

body: Fixes #3225 ## Why Scratching an itch for teams running an internally-hosted model gateway. After the 0.8.0 SSRF hardening, a provider base URL that resolves into a private/internal range (e.g. a VPN-only LiteLLM or Ollama on a `10.x` / `192.168.x` address) is hard-blocked with `Internal IPs blocked`, with no way to opt a trusted host out. The reporter (and a second commenter with the same setup) had to fall back to a brittle localhost proxy relay. The maintainer mapped out the `OD_ALLOWED_INTERNAL_HOSTS` allowlist approach in the thread and invited `/claim`. This restores the legitimate enterprise BYOK pattern while keeping the SSRF boundary intact for everything the operator did **not** explicitly trust. ## What users will see - Operators can set `OD_ALLOWED_INTERNAL_HOSTS=10.0.0.5,litellm.internal` (a daemon env var) to opt specific internal hosts out of the SSRF block. **Default (unset) changes nothing** — the strict default-deny stays for every deployment that does not opt in. - In **Settings → AI Providers**, a Base URL pointing at an internal address (e.g. `http://10.0.0.5:4000/v1`) is no longer rejected client-side with *"Use a public http:// or https:// URL."* It is accepted so the connection test / model fetch can run, and the daemon returns the authoritative allow/block decision (allowed when allowlisted, a clear `Internal IPs blocked` otherwise). ## Surface area - [x] **UI** — Settings base-URL validation relaxed for syntactically-valid internal-IP URLs (no new widget) - [x] **CLI / env var** — new `OD_ALLOWED_INTERNAL_HOSTS` - [x] **API / contract** — `packages/contracts` `validateBaseUrl` gains a `ValidateBaseUrlOptions` arg; new exported `isAllowlistedInternalHost` - [x] **Default behavior change** — internal-IP base URLs are now submittable in Settings (still blocked at the daemon unless allowlisted) ## Screenshots Settings → Execution mode → BYOK → OpenAI, with an internal endpoint `http://10.0.0.5:4000/v1` typed into the **Base URL** field. **Before** — the client rejects the internal-IP URL with *"Use a public http:// or https:// URL."*, so the operator can never reach the daemon's allowlist check: **After** — the URL is accepted (no client-side error) and the **Test** button becomes available, so the connection test / model fetch runs and the daemon returns the authoritative allow/block decision: Captured with the repo's Playwright e2e harness (headless Chromium). ## Bug fix verification Each layer was written red-first (failing on `main`, green on this branch): - `packages/contracts/tests/connection-test.test.ts` — allowlist exemption across normalized host forms + strict default-deny when empty/absent. - `apps/daemon/tests/origin-validation.test.ts` — `OD_ALLOWED_INTERNAL_HOSTS` parsing, and **malformed / CIDR entries are dropped with a warning** rather than silently trusted. - `apps/daemon/tests/connection-test.test.ts` — DNS-resolved guard honors the allowlist (literal-IP, allowlisted-hostname, and allowlisted-resolved-IP cases), non-allowlisted private targets still blocked, and the attacker-controllable asset guard **stays strict** even with an allowlist configured. - `apps/web/tests/components/SettingsDialog.test.ts` — internal-IP base URLs are UI-valid; genuinely malformed URLs still rejected. Did the tests go red on `main` and green on this branch? **yes** The allowlist is threaded into the three user-configured provider paths: connection test (`testProviderConnection`), model discovery (`listProviderModels` — the exact `Could not fetch models: Internal IPs blocked` symptom in this issue), and BYOK chat proxy/stream (`chat-routes.ts`). - **Deliberately not changed:** the attacker-controllable asset-download guard (`assertExternalAssetUrl` → `validateBaseUrlResolved` with no allowlist). Download URLs returned inside upstream responses never consult the allowlist and stay blocked. - **No CIDR support** — the matcher is exact-host. A CIDR entry (`10.0.0.0/24`) is rejected loudly rather than silently narrowed to one address, so a typo can't quietly mis-scope the guard. - Allowlisting a hostname trusts whatever it resolves to (same trade-off as `OD_ALLOWED_ORIGINS`); allowlist the resolved IP if you want the DNS-resolved address re-checked. - **Out of scope (separate pre-existing issue):** the codegen finalize handler `POST /api/projects/:id/finalize/anthropic` validates its base URL via a second `validateExternalApiBaseUrl` wrapper in `server.ts`, but the call site (`server.ts:9631`) does not `await` it — so `validated.error` is read off a pending Promise and that SSRF check is currently a no-op regardless of this change. I left it untouched rather than expand this PR into an unrelated async-correctness fix; happy to follow up separately if you'd like it threaded + awaited. ## Validation - `pnpm guard` ✓ · `pnpm typecheck` ✓ (all packages) - `pnpm --filter @open-design/contracts test` ✓ (165) - `pnpm --filter @open-design/daemon test` ✓ (full suite green; two unrelated tests — `chat-route.test.ts` OPENCODE_CONFIG and `origin-validation.test.ts` OD_WEB_PORT — are pre-existing cross-file flakes that pass in isolation) - `pnpm --filter @open-design/web test` ✓ (3221 passed, 1 skipped)

body:
## Problem

The "warming up" indicator never appeared on the overlay pill at launch, even though the model warm-up (WHISPER-127/129) runs in the background. Observed alongside the lost first dictation (WHISPER-130).

## Root cause

`LevelOverlayController` (which draws the Warming pill) subscribes to `ModelWarmupChangedMessage` in its constructor, but it is a lazily-resolved singleton **not constructed until `new LevelOverlay(...)` in `App.OnStartup` — which runs *after* `_host.Start()`**. The warm-up hosted service broadcasts `ModelWarmupChangedMessage(true)` during `_host.Start()`, before the controller is subscribed. CommunityToolkit's `WeakReferenceMessenger` does not replay, so the start is missed; the later `(false)` is a no-op (`_isWarming` already false). The pill never entered Warming.

Combined with WHISPER-130, this compounded the user-visible failure: with no warming cue, the user dictated straight into the warm-up window where the first utterance was being lost.

## Fix

Force-resolve the `LevelOverlayController` singleton between `builder.Build()` and `_host.Start()`, so its subscription is live before any hosted service runs. `new LevelOverlay(...)` later reuses the same instance.

## Test

New ordering tests (`ModelWarmupOverlayOrderingTests`) drive the **real** `ModelWarmupHostedService` and `LevelOverlayController` over a shared messenger, with the warm-up gated open so the "warming" window (true sent, not yet cleared) stays observable:

author: chaliy
body:
## What

Implements the three follow-ups left by #2140 (Workspace-as-durable-entity):

1. **Workspace fs parity** — add `move`, `copy`, and raw `download` to the
   canonical `/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/fs` surface:
   - `POST /fs/_/move`, `POST /fs/_/copy`
   - `GET /fs/_/download/{path}` (Content-Disposition: attachment)
   - `GET /fs/{path}` now also returns raw bytes for
     `Accept: application/octet-stream`
2. **`workspace_id` on the session response** — added to the core `Session`
   model (and the UI `Session` type, optional), backed by the
   `sessions.workspace_id` column, so clients read the attached workspace
   directly instead of deriving it from the session id via prefix swap.
3. **Rename** `SessionFileService` → `WorkspaceFileService` and the nine
   `*_session_file*` commands → `*_workspace_file*` (struct names + command
   identifiers, e.g. `list_session_files` → `list_workspace_files`).

OpenAPI regenerated; `specs/workspace.md` and a few spec references updated.

## Why

#2140 split Workspace out as a first-class durable entity but left the file
surface and naming half-migrated: the workspace fs lacked move/copy/download
(they lived only on the legacy session alias), the session response still
forced clients to derive the workspace id, and the internal types/commands
still read "session". These three close that gap.

## How

- The new workspace fs handlers resolve the workspace and call
  `WorkspaceFileService` directly (consistent with the existing workspace fs
  handlers), reusing the shared raw-file response helpers from the session
  routes (now `pub(crate)`).
- `Session.workspace_id` is populated through `row_to_session` from the
  `sessions.workspace_id` column, selected across all session projections.
  For the default 1:1 case it still equals the session id; shared workspaces
  (future) will diverge. The proto Session conversion reconstructs it from the
  session id under the same equality invariant.
- The rename is scoped to the service type and command structs/identifiers.
  The storage layer (`create_session_file`, `SessionFileRow`, the
  `domains/session_files` module path) and the core `SessionFile` DTO /
  `SessionFileSystem` trait are intentionally left as-is. The renamed commands
  still serve the legacy `/v1/sessions/{session_id}/fs/*` alias routes; HTTP
  paths are unchanged.

## Risk

- **Low.** No migrations, no schema change beyond reading the existing
  `sessions.workspace_id` column. New fs endpoints are additive; `workspace_id`
  is an additive response field. The one place that deserializes `Session` from
  JSON (proto conversion) was updated to populate it. The rename changes MCP
  tool identifiers for the file commands but no HTTP paths.

## Security

- **Threat categories reviewed: TM-API, TM-FS, TM-AUTHZ, TM-TENANT.**
- New fs endpoints enforce `WORKSPACE_MANAGE` (move/copy — writes, rejected on
  archived workspaces) and `WORKSPACE_VIEW` (download — read) before any DB
  call, identical to the existing workspace fs handlers. Workspace resolution
  goes through `db.get_workspace(org_id, …)`, so cross-org access is impossible
  at the storage layer (TM-TENANT).
- Path handling reuses the existing file-service validation (`..` traversal,
  null bytes, reserved `_/` prefix) and the existing Content-Disposition
  sanitization for downloads (ASCII fallback + `filename*`). No new traversal
  or injection surface.
- `workspace_id` exposure is read-only and adds no new data: the caller already
  owns the session, and the value is derivable from the session id today via
  the equality invariant.
- Command rename is mechanical; per-command policies (`SESSION_MANAGE` /
  `SESSION_VIEW`) are preserved. No new external surface, no new auth code, no
  secrets.

## Follow-ups

- **UI consumption of `workspace_id`** (stop deriving from session id) stays
  deferred until shared workspaces actually ship — the field is now exposed and
  typed (optional in TS) but the prefix-swap derivation still works under the
  1:1 invariant. Rationale: behavior-neutral until divergence is possible.
- **`domains/session_files` module path** kept as-is (only the type/commands
  renamed) to bound churn; can be renamed when the legacy session fs surface is
  fully retired.
- Workspace-scoped git / tables / KV / secrets remain open questions in
  `specs/workspace.md` (out of scope).

## Checklist

- [x] Tests added or updated (new workspace fs integration test; the workspace
  CRUD/fs routes are now wired into the test harness; command-policy +
  mcp-catalog tests updated for the new names)
- [x] Backward compatibility considered (legacy session fs routes unchanged;
  additive response field; no migrations)
- [x] Security review performed against relevant threat model categories
- [x] Final CI ran checks affected by this PR
- [x] All review comments addressed (code change or written reasoning)

## Why
The AuctionHouse platform recogniser ([#82](https://github.com/monlamltd-collab/Auction/pull/82)) correctly surfaces a whole catalogue in one scrape — **London = 844 lots, 739 newly discovered**. But every new lot is flagged `_isFirstContact`, and `enrichLotsFromLotPages` detail-fetched **all 844 before persist**. That phase never completed, so the scrape logged `recall 100%: 844/848` yet **persisted zero of them** (only the parallel hygiene wave's 104 landed). Every franchise house's first scrape would hit this wall — so the recogniser's lots never reach the UI.

Prod logs (2026-06-13 02:59):
```
Crawlee markdown recognised 739 extra lots → 844 lots (recall 100%, +739 recognised)
auctionhouseuklondon: 844/844 lots are first-contact — running deep extraction
   …(stalls; no persist)…
```

## Fix
Cap detail fetches at `DETAIL_FETCH_CAP_PER_RUN` (80) per run, neediest-first (lots missing beds). The recogniser already supplies catalogue data (address/price/image/beds/type/status), so deferred lots **persist now** and get deep-enriched (postcode/EPC/tenure/condition) over subsequent scrapes via the existing `isGapFillTarget` path + hygiene wave. Recall is unaffected — all lots persist and show; only the optional deep enrichment spreads across cycles. Overridable via `opts.maxDetailFetches`.

## 요약

절 선택 모드의 **범위 선택**을 한-손가락 슬라이드 드래그에서 **기억된 앵커(anchor) 기반 모델**로 교체합니다. 종전 슬라이드 방식은 모바일에서 패닝하는 손가락이 페이지 스크롤과 경합해 사실상 동작하지 않았습니다(끌면 화면만 스크롤됨).

## 동작

- **탭/클릭**: 단일 절 토글 + 앵커 이동. 반복 탭으로 **비연속 절** 선택(기존 유지).
- **범위 확장 (앵커→타깃, additive)**: 앵커가 기억되므로 두 끝점이 한 화면에 같이 보일 필요가 없습니다 — **시작 절 탭 → 자유 스크롤 → 끝 절 지정**.
  - **데스크탑**: 끝 절을 **Shift+클릭** (파일 탐색기·에디터 표준 관용구).
  - **모바일**: 끝 절을 **롱프레스(약 300ms 길게 누르기)** — 모바일의 "Shift" 역할.
- 손가락을 끝까지 물고 있을 필요가 없어 **화면 분량 제약이 사라지고** 스크롤 경합도 없습니다.
- 롱프레스 300ms / 드로어 "절 선택" 버튼 진입은 그대로, 진입 절이 첫 앵커가 됩니다.

## 변경 내용

- `readingContext.selectAnchor`(`string | null`) 상태 추가 — 마지막 개별 토글 절의 `data-vref`.

### R01-54 — event feeds polling contract

`argTime` now normalizes to UTC, which strips the monotonic clock reading a `time.Now()`-derived value carries. body:
Closes the one residual the #8 signing-agent security panel left open (**H1 / threat-model gap #5**) — surfaced again when I re-assessed the agent's security posture.

## The gap
`HdWallet` stored the account **xprv** long-lived. An `Xprv`'s private bytes are immutable `bytes` plus copies inside libsecp256k1's C memory, which CPython cannot overwrite in place — so `zeroize()` could only *drop the reference*, leaving a non-erasable secret resident for the entire unlock window. The seed was scrubbable; the xprv wasn't.

## The fix
`HdWallet._xprv` is now a **property that re-derives the account key from the seed per access** (`master_xprv_from_seed` → hardened `m/44'/coin'/account'`) and is **never stored**. So:
- The only resident **long-lived** secret is the BIP39 seed, which lives in a scrubbable `SecretBytes`.
- On `zeroize()` the seed is `memset` and a `_zeroized` flag makes the property **fail closed** — a locked wallet can't silently re-derive a garbage key from the now-zeroed seed.

## Why it's safe (funds-critical correctness)
`_parse_radiant_path` always normalises any configured path to the canonical `m/44'/<coin>'` shape, so the property's reconstructed path is **byte-for-byte** what `from_mnemonic`/`load` derived. A regression test proves:
- `_xprv == canonical` (and `.serialize()` equal) for coin types **512 / 0 / 236**, and per-account;
- **no `Xprv` object is stored on the instance** (only the seed + metadata);
- re-derivation is stable across accesses;
- the derivation seam **fails closed** after `zeroize`.

Every existing reader (`wallet._xprv`, the signer's `privkey_for`, the watch-only `account_xpub`, `wallet_cmds.py`) is unchanged — `_xprv` stayed the access name; only its *storage* changed. Cost is one HMAC-SHA512 + the hardened path walk per access (microseconds; fine for a CLI).

## Residual (now the irreducible floor, documented honestly)

author: kim-em
body:
This PR adds `zify`-style cast normalization of hypotheses (stage 2 of #58). The cast bucket of the Mathlib `linarith`→`lp` resurvey is dominated by goals over a ring carrier `R` (ℝ/ℚ/ℤ) whose `↑(·)` columns — cardinalities `↑(#A)`, counts, casts of `ℕ` terms — are constrained by `ℕ` hypotheses that `lp` previously dropped, because a hypothesis over a carrier different from the goal's is skipped. `linarith` lifts such facts with `zify`/`push_cast`; this is `lp`'s.

`zifyNatHyp?` (in `LP/Parse.lean`) lifts a `ℕ` comparison `a ≤ b` / `a < b` / `a = b` to the goal carrier `R` via the monotone cast — `Lean.Grind.OrderedRing.natCast_le_natCast_of_le`, `natCast_lt_natCast_of_lt`, and cast congruence for `=` — producing a proof of `↑a (rel) ↑b : R` that `collectHypProof` parses on the normal path, so the lifted `↑a`, `↑b` land on the same LP columns as the goal's casts (`findDefEqAtom` merges casts that are defeq up to the instance path).

The lift is fail-open: it runs only inside `collectHyps`' per-hypothesis `try`/`catch`, and `zifyNatHyp?` itself catches a failed cast-lemma synthesis, so a carrier lacking the monotone cast simply drops the hypothesis rather than failing the call — never a regression. lp stays sound by construction: a mis-lift makes the certificate identity fail, it never proves a false goal.

The behavioral payoff is multi-row (a lifted row constraining a goal column), so — like every multi-row case in this dependency-free suite — it is verified downstream / by the resurvey re-measurement; the repros are in comments. What `Issue58Casts.lean` validates backend-free is the part most prone to a wrong lemma name or unresolved instance: that `zifyNatHyp?` actually constructs a well-typed lifted proof, exercised directly via `run_meta` over ℤ and ℚ for each relation, and pinned by `by exact` signature checks over ℤ and an abstract `Grind` field.

`ℤ`→`R` lifting (no forward Grind monotone lemma yet) and `push_cast` of casts wrapping `ℕ` arithmetic (`↑(a + b)`) are left for a follow-up; the dominant cardinality-comparison cluster only needs the `ℕ`→`R` lift here.

Stacked on #64 (stage 1, products); this PR targets that branch for a clean diff and will retarget to `main` once #64 lands.

## frontend-dash D2 — the designed web cockpit (TASK-71)

Builds on D1 ([ADR-0032](docs/adr/0032-the-web-dash-is-a-face-on-a-local-api.md)): the intentionally-designed cockpit from a Claude Design handoff, served by `sextant dash --serve` over the verified D1 local API. The API contract is the stable boundary; this is a swappable face on it.

### What it is
An artifact-hero stage that swaps between a curated **Home**, a rendered-markdown **artifact review**, and a full **conversation** view, with a splittable/accordion **sidebar** navigator (Conversations + DMs · Artifacts by review-state · Goals · Agent status). Minimalist language: white surfaces, hairline borders, a single green live accent, black actions, Hanken Grotesk.

### Wired to the live bus
`/api/self`, `/api/clients` → agents with presence, `/api/artifacts` (+ markdown document render via marked), the SSE stream → live activity + conversation discovery, and the composer publishes real messages.

### Conventions added — layered over the core protocol, not new primitives (ADR-0033)
- **Review-state** (the brief workstream, TASK-66): a `review:{state,by,at,rev}` block in the artifact record; `POST /api/artifacts/{name}/review` (read → merge → CAS); Approve / Request-changes / Archive / Reject / Reopen; core artifact ops unchanged.
- **Per-artifact discussion**: `msg.topic.artifact.<name>`.
- **DM = a 2-party topic**: `msg.topic.dm.<sorted ids>` (distinct from the one-way inbox `msg.client.<id>`) — now the bus-wide convention.
- **Conversation discovery**: a standing `msg.>` subscription (`DeliverAll`) + `GET /api/subjects`, so the conversation list is full on load.

### Hardening
No runtime CDN: React/ReactDOM/marked vendored under `web/app/vendor/`; the JSX is precompiled to plain JS by `scripts/build-dash-ui.sh` (no in-browser Babel). `--ui <dir>` serves a live directory with `Cache-Control: no-store` for hot-reload (stable URL). `go build` embeds the committed outputs — no JS toolchain in the Go build.

### Testing
- Self-validating demo `docs/demos/dash-d2-demo.sh` — **7/7** (designed app served, no CDN/Babel, `/debug` intact, review persists state + rev, bad-state 400, subject registry, headless UI render check).
- `go test ./internal/... -race` green; e2e (`-tags e2e`) green; gofumpt + vet clean.

### Deliberately out of scope (honest gaps)
Goal metrics (stub — no primitive); the curated Home is the assistant-owned `home` artifact (hidden from the artifact list); per-message sent/received/seen is a separate protocol effort (TASK-72); a reliable "changed since approved" flag is deferred (the review write bumps the artifact revision); Google Fonts is a soft, cosmetic CDN dep (follow-up).

body:
## What

`imprnt global add/rm/list` - a real mechanism for universal behavior modules (anti-slop, a house style) to load in **every** claude session in every directory, replacing the old hack of hand-editing `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` to `@import` an absolute path into a dev checkout.

- Copies the module to a stable machine-local path `<config>/imprnt/<name>/` (never a dev-checkout pointer).
- Wires a relative `@imprnt/<name>/agent.md` import inside a **fenced, managed block** in `<config>/CLAUDE.md`. imprnt touches only the text between its two markers; the user's own global instructions are preserved.
- A bare `global add <name>` promotes an installed project plugin to global scope; `--from` takes any source dir. `rm --purge` removes the line and the copy.

Consistent with the module/capability model: scope is an install-location property, the module is unchanged, core stays blind, the litmus holds (zero core edits to add/remove).

## Safety (it edits a hand-written file)

An adversarial review found three content-loss bugs, each now fixed and regression-tested:
- CRLF files stay CRLF (no doubled carriage return at the seam) - confirmed at the byte level.
- Removing the block keeps two bracketing user paragraphs separate (no fuse).
- A block a human pasted real content into is **refused**, never overwritten.
- Path-traversal via the module name is rejected on both add and rm.

The harness/hook path (a global guard via `~/.claude/settings.json`) is specified as the next step in `docs/global-scope-plugins.md`.

## Verification

16 unit tests + 4 CLI integration tests (sandboxed via `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, never touching the real `~/.claude`). Full core suite **408 green**, typecheck + build clean.

## Qué hace

Habilita la **gestión completa de dominios `.org` desde Club Platform**, sin tener que entrar a la consola de AWS. Cubre los dos escenarios pedidos:

- **Automático** (autoservicio del club tras pagar el plan anual).
- **Manual / independiente** (admin lo hace a mano, p. ej. cuando el club paga por cheque o transferencia).

Y los tres caminos de dominio:

- 🛒 **Comprar** — registro real vía Route53 `RegisterDomain` (verifica disponibilidad + precio en tiempo real).
- 🔗 **Conectar** — dominio que el club ya tiene en otro proveedor → se enlaza a Vercel y se entregan las instrucciones DNS.
- 🔄 **Transferir** — `TransferDomain` con código de autorización (EPP).

Todos los dominios quedan **forzados a `.org`**. Al completarse el registro/transferencia, el DNS se apunta automáticamente a Vercel.

## Cambios

**Backend**
- `server/services/DomainProvisioningService.js` — reescrito como motor completo: `checkAvailability`, `getPrice` (ListPrices .org), `registerDomain`, `transferDomain`, `connectDomain`, `getOperationStatus` (finaliza DNS al quedar `SUCCESSFUL`), `provisionDns` (usa la Hosted Zone autocreada en vez de crear una nueva — corrige el bug del borrador previo) e integración con `VercelService`. Contacto WHOIS configurable por env (`DOMAIN_CONTACT_*`).
- `server/routes/domains.js` — nuevos endpoints `/price`, `/register`, `/transfer`, `/connect`, `/operation/:id`; `/check` ahora valida `.org` y adjunta precio. Operaciones con costo protegidas por rol (`administrator`, `club_admin`, `district_admin`).

**Frontend**
- `src/components/admin/DomainManager.tsx` — modal autónomo con los 3 modos (Comprar / Conectar / Transferir), verificación de disponibilidad + precio, y seguimiento del estado de la operación.
- `src/pages/admin/Clubs.tsx` — botón "Registrar / Conectar dominio" en la ficha del club que abre el modal.

**Versionado** — bump a `v4.438.0` (`package.json`, `package-lock.json`, `SystemUpdates.tsx`, log de arranque del router de dominios).

## ⚠️ Notas antes de hacer merge / pasar a ready

body:
<!-- # fix(starlarktest): harden ### annotation matching harness -->

<!-- Remove unnecessary sections to keep the review focused -->

## Related Links

- Issues
  - Closes <https://github.com/connect0459/starlark-mbt/issues/161>
- PRs
  - N/A

## [Required] Overview

Four latent correctness gaps in the `###`-based error-matching harness are
fixed. Each gap is addressed in a separate commit.

### `\.` now matches a literal dot

The mini-regex engine stripped backslashes during a pre-processing step, turning
`\.` into `.` (wildcard). Patterns like `"int\.float"` would therefore match
`"int_float"` as well as `"int.float"`. Backslash escapes are now handled inline
during matching; the pre-processing step is removed.

A new `effective_pattern_length` helper counts the number of text characters a
pattern consumes (each `\X` pair consumes one text character), which is also
used to correctly bound the sliding-window search in `find_mini_pattern`.

### Malformed `###` annotations are reported as test errors

A `###` annotation whose content is neither a double-quoted string nor a
backtick-quoted string (e.g. `### some-bare-text` or `### "unclosed`) was
silently treated as no annotation. Such lines now produce an explicit failure
with the message `malformed ### annotation: <raw>`.

A new discriminant type (`HashAnnotation`) replaces the previous `String?`
return value from annotation parsing, making the three cases
(`NoAnnotation`, `Malformed`, `ValidPattern`) unambiguous at the call site.

### Errors matched by exact line number; all annotations must be consumed

Previously, an error was considered matched if *any* annotation in the chunk
matched its message, regardless of which line the error occurred on. This
allowed annotations and errors to be matched across lines — starlark-go
requires an exact line match.

`run_chunked_string` now keys each `###` annotation by its 1-based line number
within the chunk. When a runtime error is raised, its origin line is resolved
from the call stack (innermost frame first, mirroring starlark-go's
`CallStack.At(0) = innermost` convention) and falls back to parsing the
`"<test>:LINE:"` prefix from the message for syntax/resolve errors.

An error matches an annotation only when both occur on the same line. Any
annotation with no matching error and any error on a line with no annotation
are both reported as failures (all-consume semantics).

### Compiler: `SetDictUniq` now records the key's source position

As a prerequisite for exact line-number matching in dict literals, the compiler
was updated to emit `SetDictUniq` with the key expression's position rather than
the dict literal's opening `{`. This means runtime errors (unhashable key,
duplicate key) now point at the offending entry, matching starlark-go's
behaviour.

- [x] `internal/compile` package

## Schema (\`20260613120000_org_teams.sql\`)

- **\`retros.org_team_id\`** + **\`rooms.org_team_id\`** — nullable FKs with \`ON DELETE SET NULL\` so an archived team doesn't cascade through artefacts.

body:
Fixes #16.

DuckDB returns `UUID` columns as `uuid.UUID` and `INTERVAL` as `datetime.timedelta`, neither of which `CustomJSONEncoder` handled — so `.json` on any row with a UUID column 500'd with *"Object of type UUID is not JSON serializable"*. `sqlite3` returns these as plain strings, so the SQLite backend never hit it.

### Fix
Handle both in `CustomJSONEncoder.default` alongside the existing `date`/`datetime`/`Decimal`/`bytes` cases (the same class of DuckDB-native-type gap), rather than coercing in the DuckDB backend. This keeps the real typed value flowing through the system and fixes serialization for any backend.

```python
if isinstance(obj, datetime.timedelta):
    return str(obj)
...
if isinstance(obj, uuid.UUID):
    return str(obj)
```

### Verification
- Unit: added UUID + INTERVAL cases to `test_custom_json_encoder`; full `tests/test_utils.py` passes (189).
- End-to-end: with the patched core, `/lm20/filing/147963.json` returns 200 (was 500), the UUID column renders as a JSON string, and `.csv` export works.

Found via a real-traffic replay of labordata.bunkum.us against the SQLite and DuckDB deployments (69 distinct URLs / 414 hits).
